item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Russia is expanding its influence in Africa, supplying fighter jets and air-defence systems to Ethiopia while President Putin promotes Russia as a partner to the continent. In Ukraine, a US-brokered ceasefire in Oleshky continues and demining work is creating a humanitarian corridor, while Russian drones have killed a Canadian volunteer in Donetsk and struck Moscow, grounding flights. Investigators have concluded that Russia committed war crimes by targeting civilians, and 75,767 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

Israeli strikes in Gaza this week killed 21 people, according to the Health Ministry. Israeli settlers have assaulted activists and journalists in the occupied West Bank. The parliamentary election remains deadlocked, with Netanyahu's bloc leading but short of a majority and a record Arab turnout, while the conflict produced 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iran and the regional confrontation: the situation
item.description:
Iran is pressing Qatar to reopen the Strait of Hormuz while Houthi missiles and drones continue striking Saudi oil facilities and airports, prompting the reopening of Riyadh Airport after weeks of disruption. The United States has lost roughly 25% of its Reaper drones as the war depletes its arsenal and is weighing renewed strikes on Iran, driving oil prices above $117 a barrel. JD Vance has contacted a senior Iranian official to revive peace talks, and Qatar has urged Iran to end threats as a goodwill step. 123 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Yemen and the Red Sea: the situation
item.description:
Houthi forces have struck Yemen's Aden airport and launched a ballistic missile toward Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, while Saudi-led coalition aircraft have bombed a market in northern Yemen and a petrol station, causing civilian casualties. Saudi civil defense intercepted a Houthi missile over the Eastern Province and the coalition reported intercepting additional missiles. Aden airport has reopened after the Houthi attack, and the coalition continues airstrikes that killed 12 people in a residential area. The conflict caused 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
Jordan has resumed airstrikes in southern Syria against Daesh militants, prompting Syrian authorities to condemn the raids as a breach of airspace and to report civilian casualties. Syrian security forces killed a French jihadist in a shootout in Harem and another French fighter in Idlib, while unidentified gunmen killed two Syrian defence ministry personnel in Idlib. The two sides have reopened the Nasib border crossing and agreed to a joint security committee and investigation into the strikes. The conflict produced 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iraq: the situation
item.description:
Iraqi courts sentenced three French ISIS members to life terms, while a separate court sentenced an MP over oil contracts, showing continued legal actions against militants and corruption. Security forces downed an unidentified drone over Baghdad and coordinated with the Kurdistan Region on weapons control, reflecting heightened air-space security. Prime Minister Al-Zaidi pressed Damascus on border security and oil links during a visit to Syria, linking regional diplomacy to Iraq's internal security agenda. Baghdad will host the 2028 OIC anti-corruption meeting, marking a new diplomatic role for the capital. The conflict produced 396 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Sudan's civil war: the situation
item.description:
RSF drone strikes have hit Darfur markets, killing more than 100 civilians and have also struck a power station, cutting electricity to two states. The Sudanese army is accused of launching 162 drone attacks from Ethiopian territory, while Ethiopia denies involvement. Women are increasingly serving as frontline responders as the siege worsens and civilian arrests rise. Nearly 120,000 people have been displaced in Blue Nile state since January, according to a UN agency. The conflict caused 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

The SSPDF and SPLA-IO forces clashed in Wij-Panyikang, Upper Nile, and the UN commission warned that the peace deal is being dismantled. item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:
Al Shabaab fighters are clashing with Turkish-trained Somali troops in Lower Shabelle and ambushing units near Baidoa, while a former al-Shabaab finance chief was killed in a joint operation by Somali intelligence and security forces in the same region. African Union peacekeepers are withdrawing from four bases in Lower Shabelle, and the UN political mission in Somalia has ended without a replacement to address the unresolved election dispute. Ethiopia has received Russian fighter jets, with S‑400 air-defence systems slated to follow, indicating a new external military dimension. The conflict caused 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Nigeria: the situation
item.description:

Bandits seized logistics supplies in Benue and attempted abductions in Zamfara, where troops rescued two herders and recovered livestock, and in Sokoto where troops foiled a terrorist ambush. Military operations destroyed a bomb-making hideout in Borno, killed 15 terrorists and two ISWAP commanders, and neutralised 44 terrorists in another Borno strike. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo have risen above 10,000, and a nurse treating patients was killed by a mob while another health worker was wounded.
